digo: Mfidzofidzo; Mfunga sandzu (also Kisambwe, Mfunga tanzu)
digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005

teaser.en: Its branches grow in threes, perfect for the three-pronged stick used to stir porridge, and the tree is named after it.

summary.en: *Mfidzofidzo*, the African mangosteen, is an evergreen tree whose orange fruit is one of the most delicious wild fruits of the coast. Its branches, growing in threes, give the stirring stick that names the tree.

about.en:
*Mfidzofidzo* is an evergreen tree of 2 to 10 metres with a heavy, cone-shaped crown. Its branches typically grow in threes, all from one point, and its stiff, leathery leaves grow in pairs or threes.

Cut the bark and a yellow-red latex oozes out. The fruits are round and bright orange, with thin skin and juicy, sweet-sour flesh.

where.en: It grows in riverine forest, in thicket and on rocky outcrops. Look for its dark, conical crown and its branches arranged in threes.

uses.en:
The fruit is one of the most delicious wild fruits of the coast and is eaten fresh.

The three-pronged twigs are made into sticks for stirring porridge. The wood is also used for poles and spoons, the root is used in medicine, and the bark gives a dye.

culture.en: Pakia explains that the name *mfidzofidzo* comes from *lifidzo*, the three-pronged stirring stick made from its branches. It is a tree named for the kitchen tool it provides.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo names *mfidzofidzo* and *mfunga sandzu*, also *kisambwe* and *mfunga tanzu*. In Swahili it is *mpekechu*, *mpeketo* or *mtotozi*. In Giriama it is *mufodzohi*. In English it is the African mangosteen or imbe, and its scientific name is *Garcinia livingstonei*.

reason.en: A close relative in the same plant order, with similar latex
Another favourite wild fruit of the coast
Another wild fruit tree of riverbanks

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
